title: Can a knot match its mirror?
hook: Hold a rope trefoil up to a mirror. Can you ever make the rope match its reflection?

knows: what a mirror image is, and that a trefoil is a closed loop with three crossings
doesNotKnow: that turning a knot over is a way of moving it, so it never changes the knot, while its mirror image can be a different knot: no wiggling turns the left-handed trefoil into the right-handed one. The figure-eight is its own mirror image.

misconception: A mirror image is the same knot; you just flip it over.
objective: The learner can explain that turning the trefoil over leaves every crossing mark the same, so it is the same knot, while the mirror changes every mark, and that the trefoil cannot be moved into its mirror image.
keyState: Two milestones on the trefoil: 'turned' (card turned over at rest, on either side of the mirror: W-1606) and 'mirrored' (mirrored on either face, marks +,+,+, Sum +3). The seen line 'Trefoil: turned over −3 · mirror +3' is never cleared; its 'turned over' segment is written only from the plain turned state (unmirrored, marks −,−,−, Sum −3), its 'mirror' segment at the first mirrored rest. Optional, not on the QA path: 'eightMirror' (figure-eight mirrored, Sum 0).

claims.text: Turning a knot over in your hands is a way of moving it, so it does not change the knot; the mirror is a reflection, not a move ('turning over is a way of moving it, so its hand stayed left'; branch when the plain turned state was never reached: 'Turning the mirrored trefoil over left every mark plus: turning over is a way of moving it, so its hand stayed right.'; 'turning one over never swaps them'; recall answer 'A right-handed trefoil').
claims.source: Fielden, Leigh, Woltering, 'Molecular Knots', Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2017 (PMC5582600): glossary 'Chiral knot' and section 2.4 (deformation without the strand passing through itself); amphichiral definition in PMC8199745. Brief claim 6. Builder-written; unverified.
claims.note: Lane left-or-right v3 (fact-checker, 2026-10-17, base 8a67fe3e; a fresh instance that did not write this claim or draft the branch wording): VERIFIED. Own argument: turning over is the rotation by 180 degrees about an axis in the page; rotations by angle s in [0, 180] are a continuous family of rigid motions, so the knot is carried along without the strand passing through itself, while a reflection reverses the orientation of space and lies in no such family. Own computation: a kit-free 3D torus trefoil keeps its crossing signs -,-,- when rotated 180 degrees about an in-page axis and reads +,+,+ when reflected; reflected then rotated stays +,+,+; on the kit 3_1 PD own turn-over and mirror give the same (own.py). So the branch 'Turning the mirrored trefoil over left every mark plus: turning over is a way of moving it, so its hand stayed right.' holds: the mirrored trefoil (+3) turned over is still +3, and hand(+3) is 'Right-handed' (Demo.tsx hand()). Opened PMC5582600 (OAI full text): sec. 2.4 'knot projections can be deformed as much as desired (without the strand passing through itself) and knots are only topologically chiral if they cannot be deformed continuously to superimpose with their mirror image'; glossary 'Chiral knot A knot that cannot be continuously deformed into its mirror image'; sec. 2.1 'Positive crossings describe a right-handed helix, negative crossings a left-handed helix'. PMC8199745 amphichiral definition as quoted in the v2 note (not re-opened). Rendered text: branch sentence present only when seen.turned is undefined, standard otherwise, on all 114 unlocking press sequences up to 6 presses (render.cjs, Reveal rendered unchanged from Demo.tsx); 'turning one over never swaps them' on both paths; recall answer index 0 'A right-handed trefoil' in meta.json. Not run in a browser by me (two-server cap; running servers hold older builds); the builder's Chromium probe reports the same openers. The hand word 'right' in the branch rests on c5's convention; c5 must add 'its hand stayed right' to its quotes (see record). Record: company/reviews/left-or-right/2026-10-17-fact-check-v3.md; own scripts company/reviews/left-or-right/fc-2026-10-17-v3/ (own.py, render.cjs). recall.question: You hold a right-handed trefoil made of rope. You turn it upside down and lay it flat. What do you have?
options: Either, depending on how you lay it
recall.why: Turning a knot over is a way of moving it, and moving never changes the knot. Only a mirror image swaps the trefoil's hand, and no move reaches it.
